region: Union Springs · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Tom and Susan Higgins founded Heart & Hands in the mid-2000s with one goal: to grow Burgundy’s grapes on limestone in the Finger Lakes. After years of studying geological maps, they settled on a slope above Cayuga Lake’s eastern shore near Union Springs, built their winery in 2008 and opened the tasting room in 2009. Tom, a Finger Lakes native who trained in New York retail, in Bordeaux and in local cellars, makes the wine and runs the vineyard. Susan, an NYU Stern MBA, runs the business.

The winery first made Chardonnay in 2017. The grapes are hand-picked and basket-pressed, and the juice is fermented in separate lots by vineyard block, clone and vessel. For the 2020, Decanter’s listing describes ageing in standard and large-format French oak barrels with regular stirring of the lees, a Burgundian technique that adds texture. The wine is dry, at 13.2% alcohol, and like the winery’s other bottles it is sealed with a Vino-Lok glass stopper.

Heart & Hands rates 2020 among its finest vintages: a dry early summer and a warm, sunny autumn let the team pick every block at full ripeness. Its own note describes chalky minerality, key lime and green apple on the nose, with citrus carrying onto the palate alongside apricot and fresh cream, finishing dry and crisp.
